questions.question: Distinguish between mass and weight, giving the unit and measuring instrument for each.
questions.expected_answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms with a balance; it does not change with location. Weight is the gravitational force on an object, measured in newtons with a spring balance; it depends on the gravitational field strength.

questions.question: Calculate the weight of a 60 kg astronaut on Earth (g = 9,8 N/kg) and on the Moon (g = 1,6 N/kg), and state the astronaut's mass on the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: Earth: W = m × g = 60 × 9,8 = 588 N. Moon: 60 × 1,6 = 96 N. Mass on the Moon: 60 kg (unchanged).

questions.question: Explain why astronauts in the International Space Station appear weightless even though gravity acts on them.
questions.expected_answer: Gravity there is still about 90 percent of its surface value. The astronauts and the station are in free fall together, continuously falling around the Earth, so nothing pushes up on the astronauts and they float relative to the station.
